title: Peter Drucker's Single Question for Cleaning Out Dead Commitments
alt_title_1: The 1964 Abandonment Test for Your Half-Year Wealth & Time Audit
alt_title_2: How One Question Defeats Status Quo Bias Every Six Months
description_hook: In his 1964 classic Managing for Results, Peter Drucker introduced systematic abandonment with one piercing test: 'If we were not already in this today, knowing what we now know, would we enter it now?' Here is your 20-minute half-year audit.

scenes.headline: One 1964 Sentence That Frees Months of Margin
scenes.stat_label: TWENTY MINUTES TO PRUNE SIX MONTHS OF DRIFT
bullets: Works on subscriptions, meetings, and dead holdings
scenes.narration: One sentence from 1964 clears more dead weight from your calendar and portfolio in twenty minutes than any productivity app ever built.
scenes.source: Peter F. Drucker, Managing for Results (1964)

scenes.headline: Peter Drucker's Systematic Abandonment Test
bullets: 'Knowing what we know now, would we enter this today?'
Strips away historical inertia in five seconds
scenes.narration: In his 1964 book Managing for Results, Peter Drucker taught executives systematic abandonment through one test: 'If we were not already in this today, knowing what we now know, would we enter it now?'
scenes.source: Peter F. Drucker, Managing for Results (1964)

scenes.headline: Yesterday's Commitments Starve Tomorrow's Winners
scenes.left_body: Keeps stale projects & zombie bills purely out of habit
scenes.right_body: Exits every 'No' cleanly -> concentrates hours on 10x bets
scenes.narration: Without scheduled abandonment, yesterday's lukewarm meetings, stale side projects, and forgotten subscriptions quietly eat the margin needed for tomorrow's best opportunities.

scenes.headline: Schedule a Clean Exit Whenever the Answer Is No
scenes.stat_label: RECLAIMED CAPITAL & HOURS COMPOUND IN HIGHER-RETURN ASSETS
scenes.stat_subtext: Audit calendar + bills + portfolio every June & December
scenes.narration: Run Drucker's question every six months across your calendar, bills, and holdings: wherever the honest answer is no, schedule a clean exit date immediately.

scenes.headline: Prune Twice a Year to Compound Faster
scenes.stat_label: CLEAR DEAD WOOD BEFORE STARTING NEXT QUARTER
bullets: Never defend a commitment just because you started it
Reinvest freed hours directly into owned assets
scenes.narration: Prune dead commitments twice a year so your capital and focus stay concentrated on real compounders.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin half-year audit based on Peter Drucker (1964)
